title: late-shift-install-log-and-customer-workarounds-2026-09-27
body:
Late-shift install log — Tuesday 2026-09-27
Owners on shift: Marcus (lead), Priya (network), Diego (ops), Elena (customer liaison)
Context: Night window for Orion Health onprem cluster (3-node GPU private deployment). Goal was finalize day-2 KV cache tuning, finish cert rotation, and close out NFS tuning JIRA.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Primary blocker: persistent NFS mount flakiness on customer kernel 5.4 variant causing intermittent model pulls and broken container start sequences.
- Secondary: unexpected TLS leaf cert mismatch between customer edge LB and installer-ca path — caused autoupdate to skip service reload.
- Workarounds implemented: temporary bind-mount to local SSD for model pulls (reduces NFS reads), explicit systemd restart sequence post-cert-copy.
- Impact: ~30 minutes of degraded throughput for the live inference queue; no customer data loss, but two canary nodes reported slow responses and were manually drained.

Timeline / Notes: (rough, notes-to-self style)
- 21:15 — initial alert: canary-1 stuck in CrashLoopBackOff pulling model shard (image pull completed, container failed during init).
- 21:18 — Diego confirmed repeated "I/O timeout" on /mnt/models (NFS) in kubelet logs.
- 21:25 — Priya ran showmount -e against the NAS; exports looked normal. Packet captures (tcpdump) indicated bursts of retransmits and server-side high iowait.
- 21:40 — Attempted remount with vers=3,rsize=65536,wsize=65536,soft,timeo=600,retrans=2 — transiently improved, then symptoms returned at 22:05.
- 22:10 — Risk decision: avoid broad changes to customer NAS config overnight. Implemented local-bind workaround: rsync hot model shards to /local-ssd/models and changed kube mount for canary pods to use local path via node-affinity. Restored canary throughput by 22:28.
- 22:35 — While restoring canary, cert-rotation job failed to reload gateway: systemctl reload redwood-gateway returned status 1. Logs showed certificate chain validation failed: installer copied intermediate cert to /etc/ssl/intermediate.crt but LB expected combined-chain.pem.
- 22:50 — Manual concatenation of certs and restart succeeded. Noted mismatch in installer templates where we write certs to two different locations depending on distro (ubuntu vs rhel). Created quick patch to template to unify path for this customer (applied to host via ansible).
- 23:10 — Observed a regression: model-serving process had increased CPU jitter after bind workaround; traced to sidecar telemetry writing to same local SSD and causing I/O spikes. Disabled telemetry writes to disk for canaries until morning.
- 23:40 — Confirmed customer-facing endpoints back to baseline SLA (p95 latency within 1.2x normal), informed Orion oncall (Elena).

Root cause hypotheses and evidence:
- NFS server is overloaded under concurrent shard pulls. Evidence: high iowait, retransmits, NFS server export metrics. We did not rule out TCP window/bottleneck on customer SAN network (their switch has known bufferbloat in older firmware).
- Installer cert template inconsistency: two different relative paths in our distro recipes led to occasional deployments where the gateway picks wrong chain file. Evidence: template diff between installer-ubuntu.j2 and installer-rhel.j2 (see linked confluence).

Immediate actions taken (short-lived fixes):
- Bind-mount to local SSD for model shards on canary nodes (temporary, controlled).
- Manual cert concat + systemd restart.
- Disabled disk-backed telemetry for affected pods.

Open/next actions (owners and ETA):
- PD-1842 (Priya): Run switch bufferbloat test with customer networking team and validate MTU/profile. ETA 2026-09-29.
- PD-1847 (Diego): Make local-bind workaround an idempotent option in the install shim (feature flag), add smoke test. ETA 2026-10-04.
- PD-1851 (Marcus): Unify cert path template across distros and add unit test to installer pipeline to validate chain presence. ETA 2026-10-01.
- PD-1855 (Elena): Coordinate with Orion for a controlled NAS load test window; capture NFS server metrics (iostat, nfsstat) during model fan-out. ETA 2026-10-02.

Notes / questions to follow up (notes-to-self):
- Can we add a lightweight local caching proxy in the runtime to avoid full model shard fan-out to NFS? Prototype idea: small LRUDisk cache that prefetches top-K shards. Would reduce peak NFS pressure but needs eviction guarantees. (Ping eng-serving-runtime)
- How often do cert-template mismatches happen? Add a preflight validation step that verifies combined-chain.pem read by gateway after certs are distributed.
- Telemetry sidecar writing to same SSD is a product placement bug — consider writing to tmpfs for smaller payloads or rotating to /var/log on a different disk.

Communication / customer-facing notes (short):
- Notifying Orion: summary sent at 23:55 (Elena) — "We implemented a temporary local cache to stabilize model pulls and applied a cert fix. We recommend a controlled NAS performance window before making permanent changes."
- Internal ops broadcast: #install-run: short postmortem and action list posted.

Retro / quick learnings: (for sprint doc)
- Add an install preflight check for NFS health: verify average read latencies and export retransmit counters.
- Installer should fail safe if cert chain lookup ambiguous — prefer explicit combined file creation step during rotation.
- Night windows: keep one ops engineer focused on telemetry/sidecars to catch secondary I/O effects.

Attachments / artifacts referenced: JIRA PD-1842 (NFS investigation), PD-1851 (cert template fix), Confluence runbook link in linked_artifacts above.

Status: draft — will convert to in_review after PD-1851 patch is merged and we have initial NAS metrics from Orion.

-- end of log --

Notes to self: remember to update the installer release notes with the cert-path unification and the new install-toggle for local-bind.
